data.hypothesis: The measured parent uses __reduce_add_sync for int warp sums and is correct, but its whole-call timing does not isolate that intrinsic's contribution. Removing only that specialization tests the same mapping, 128-thread blocks, shared-memory inter-warp combination, launch/pass structure, and zero-padded tails using the generic five-step shuffle-down reduction instead. The shuffle version should remain correct with all lanes participating; whether it is faster than the intrinsic path is unknown and requires the controller's repeated whole-call measurements.

memory_lessons.applicability: This T2 experiment contrasts the int warp primitive while holding the parent's block reduction topology and call structure fixed.
memory_lessons.claim: The parent warp-reduction candidate was correct on all 10 tested cases and measured 30.015 µs mean versus the baseline's 47.079 µs. Because the candidate changed the intra-block tree as a whole, those measurements do not attribute the difference to __reduce_add_sync specifically.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this shuffle-only variant's correctness and repeated whole-call timings with the measured parent; attribute any timing difference cautiously to the changed primitive under the otherwise matching source.

data.notes: Only the int-specific __reduce_add_sync specialization is removed; the generic shuffle-down helper is used instead. The controller must establish correctness and measure repeated whole-call timings. No combination speedup is claimed.
transformations: Remove the architecture-specific int specialization so int reductions use the existing generic __shfl_down_sync loop.
Keep the zero-padded input mapping, 128-thread launch, per-warp shared-memory partials, CTA barrier, inter-warp warp-0 reduction, pass loop, scratch selection, and output copy unchanged.
